whatItFakes: The state-chamber party-loyalty weight (weights.statePartyLoyalty, 1) is checked against the federal party-unity figure (about 0.90, CQ Vote Studies) because the state roll-call calibration input is not in the repository.
why: The owner ruled on Oct 15 that his own state roll-call input may calibrate this one parameter, with nothing from it shipped or cited; a builder session does not hold that input.
replacement: Run the owner's state roll-call input against the simulated chambers (src/core2/party-loyalty.test.ts measures them), set statePartyLoyalty and the test's target from it, and close this row.

whatItFakes: A state's grocery exemption spares groceries from every level's sales tax in the town, as if every state's local sales taxes followed the state's base. A county's or city's exemption spares only its own tax.
why: No place data says which states let local sales taxes still reach groceries the state exempts (for example home-rule cities, or local option taxes kept on food), so the engine takes the common case of a uniform base.
replacement: A per-state field in the starting-law research (data/research/laws/local-starting-law/sales-tax.json) saying whether local sales taxes follow the state's grocery exemption, sourced from each state's revenue department, read here so a state exemption spares only the levels its base covers.

whatItFakes: A lobbying ban with no numeric period on its law row retains the existing estimated two-year cooling-off period. Researched numeric periods are read from the actual law instead.
why: Some researched yes answers have no structured period, and a newly enacted yes/no bill can omit a duration. This item fixes continuous service and reads available provisions without inventing missing statutory detail.
replacement: Supply the missing structured periods through researched starting-law and voted bill provisions; remove the fallback when every applicable ban carries one.
